title: Session checkpointing and reassembly for hosted SSE to reduce partial output loss
creator: Aisha Banerjee
description:
Summary: Several hosted API customers observed truncated or duplicated streaming responses after mid-stream transient failures (connection resets, proxy timeouts). This ticket implements a server-side session checkpointing and reassembly mechanism so clients can transparently resume and receive a consistent, de-duplicated final output.

Problem details: In the current flow the runtime emits token chunks over SSE and a lightweight connection state is kept in-memory on the serving node. On transient disconnects (LB timeout, worker restart, short GC), the client reconnects but the previous in-flight tokens are lost or partially re-emitted, producing truncated outputs or duplicates. PayCore (fintech customer) and one hosted chat app escalated after they saw user-facing truncations and incorrect deterministic prompts.

Goals:
- Guarantee that a resumed stream can reconstruct the logical output up to the last acknowledged token without duplication.
- Keep latency impact minimal for normal low-failure paths.
- Provide a clear fallback path (non-streaming finalization) when resume fails.

Design highlights:
1) Ephemeral session checkpoint store: on start of a streaming response the runtime allocates a session_id and writes incremental checkpoints (last_token_index, KV-cache pointer, partial-chunk-hash) to a fast central store (Redis cluster with AOF & 30s replication). Checkpoints are append-only and compacted after stream completion.
2) Resume token: server returns short opaque resume_token at regular intervals (every N chunks) and on disconnects. Clients include resume_token when reconnecting to assert resume point. Token encodes session_id + checkpoint_seq + HMAC.
3) Reassembly service: a lightweight reassembly module runs in front of the runtime: when a reconnect request arrives with a resume_token it verifies the checkpoint, replays token deltas (from the checkpointed offset) and streams the remainder; the runtime will deduplicate already-emitted token ranges using the checkpoint index.
4) Fallback: if checkpoint verification fails (TTL expired or store unavailable), the server will return a short metadata event instructing the client to open a non-streaming completion call (single response) with the same request_id to obtain the full final text.
5) Backpressure & cost control: checkpoints are throttled (configurable frequency) and buffered persistently only for sessions with duration > X seconds or token_count > Y to control write amplification.

Implementation plan:
- Runtime change: add checkpoint writer + session allocator (patch: runtime/session-checkpointing).
- Proxy change: add resume-token handshake in streaming proxy (patch: proxy/stream-resume-handshake).
- Store infra: small Redis cluster (managed) and migration script; feature guarded behind runtime flag `sse.checkpointing.enabled`.
- Client SDK update: add auto-resume logic and resume-token header; backward-compatible when server doesn't set resume_token.

Rollout and verification:
- Nightly integration test that kills serving node mid-stream and verifies resumed stream matches original complete output.
- Canary rollout to 5% of hosted traffic (non-enterprise customers) with telemetry gates.
- Metrics to watch: resumed_stream_success_rate, resumed_duplicate_token_rate, resume_latency_ms, fallbacks_to_non_streaming_count.
- Customer communication: notify PayCore and the reporting customers with ETA and opt-in canary details.

Risks and mitigations:
- Redis outage could prevent resume; mitigated with fallback non-streaming finalization and degraded-mode where the server emits a full final response on reconnect.
- Storage write QPS cost increase; mitigated by checkpoint throttling and adaptive sampling.
- Security: resume_token must be HMACed and short TTL. No PII stored in checkpoints.

Success criteria:
- >95% of resumed streams complete without duplicate or missing content in canary group.
- PayCore confirms end-user incidents resolved in their next release cycle.

Related artifacts: design doc, PR, and dashboards listed in 'links'.
